messages:
maya: Heads up — we got a support ticket where customer A sees mid-inference 5xx failures during a regional maintenance window. They were pinned to region-us-west, then ~30s into a long generation the requests started returning 503 and the session seemed routed to eu-west. Link: https://support/internal/INC-5523 :grimacing:

infra-bot: ALERT region-us-west: 503_spike (5m avg 3.2% -> 18%), connection-reset count up 420 in last 10m. Related deploy: none.

oliver: Can you paste sample request/response? Curious if sticky cookie or conntrack is being lost.

rae: Reproduced locally by draining a node in a regional pool while running multi-chunk generation. Observed that client gets a DNS answer for eu-west after LB returns 200+Set-Cookie for sticky but conntrack entries are gone so upstream rejects.

sam: Repro steps I used:
```bash
# start long generation, then trigger region drain
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDBWOOD" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"<big prompt>"}' \
  https://api.us.example.com/v1/generate | tee /tmp/resp.txt
# headers show:
# Set-Cookie: rw_session=abcd; Path=/; HttpOnly
# X-Region: us-west
```
Then after drain the same client made the next chunk request and got 302 -> eu-west and the socket got reset. Response body: `{"error":"region_mismatch","code":503}`

oliver: can you share conntrack stats from the node that drained? suspect nf_conntrack evictions at the same time as LB reassign.

sam: Got this from the node being drained: 
```text
# conntrack -S
entries 98512
searched 12345
found 98000
lost 512
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 100000
# dmesg shows: conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```

oncall: Also noticed ALB logs show cookie being reset when the target group scaled from 4->6. ALB doesn't persist the sticky cookie across the handoff because cookie domain is host-level and we have geo-DNS resolving to different hostnames. Client DNS TTL was 10s at the time so clients did quick re-resolve.

maya: Hypothesis: two mechanisms combined: (1) conntrack table full causes in-flight TCP resets, (2) DNS TTL + LB scale/rebind leads client to new region host which can't reconcile sticky cookie or TCP state, causing mid-session failures. That matches the timing in support logs.

rae: Proposed mitigations (short-term):
- increase nf_conntrack_max by 50% on edge NATs and draining nodes
- set ALB sticky cookie domain to the regional host (not shared global)
- temporarily bump DNS TTL to 30s during maintenance windows
- add a server-side handshake: if X-Region header mismatches session cookie, respond with 409 and include `x-session-handoff: warm-pool` so client can retry to same region

oliver: Long-term: consistent-hash per session at LB layer or per-route affinity using the session token instead of relying on conntrack. Also we should add a warm pool in each region that honors old session cookies during rollouts.

sam: I can run the conntrack bump + smoke test in staging now. Commands I'll run: 
```bash
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
# restart minimal edge agent to pick it up
sudo systemctl restart edge-proxy
# run synthetic long-gen for 10m while draining a node
```
I'll report results in ~30m.

infra-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE applied to staging: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000 by sam at 1993000600.

oncall: If staging looks good we should roll to prod with a canary (10% of traffic) and monitor: 5xx rate, conntrack entries, LB cookie churn. I'll prepare a runbook.

maya: Assignments: sam -> staging + canary, oliver -> LB sticky cookie config + consistent-hash eval, rae -> DNS TTL strategy + client retry handshake, oncall -> runbook + monitoring thresholds. Please add updates here. :thumbsup:

rae: Also adding a note: let's not reduce DNS TTL below 10s in general; only bump up during maint windows. We should document the client retry semantics so SDKs can respect x-session-handoff.

oliver: Agreed. Also we should check GPU job controllers — some long-running inferences were canceled because connection reset propagated to runtime and aborted the job. We need the runtime to be resilient to short control-plane reconnects.

maya: Good catch. Add runtime team to follow-up. If customer impact > 1% we'll open a postmortem.

sam: Staging run done — no 503s during drain with conntrack bump and cookie change. Will open prod canary PR now.

infra-bot: CANARY_DEPLOY started for prod (10% traffic) by sam at 1993003000.

oncall: Monitoring looks okay so far (10m): 5xx at 0.6% baseline -> 0.9% canary (within alert thresholds). Proceeding to 50% if stable.

maya: Thanks all — keep updates here and we'll sync in 20 if canary passes. :rocket:
